attribution_limitations: Hemoglobin discrepancy, not a source conflict: the text prints 9.1 g/dL on admission, while Table 1 prints 12.2 g/dL for hospitalization day 1 (9 g/dL on day 3; 9.1 appears nowhere in the table). The source never states that the admission sample is the Day 1 row, so the two are kept as separate scored values.

Source conflict on the C-reactive protein unit only: the text prints mg/dL (113.1, later 212, 16.8 at discharge) while the Table 1 header prints mg/L (113.1, 212.1, 16.8 among its values). The CRP values stay scored without a unit; the unit is quarantined in two review_only facts. Text and table values are not merged (212 vs 212.1 would otherwise be a rounding difference).
The text prints urea 12.9 mmol/L twice at discharge, the second time with the unit misspelled "mml/L".
D-dimer unit is printed as ng/mL for the first value and ng/dL for the later value.

Text values introduced with "later", "then" or "further decreased" are not tied to a hospital day, and the first-listed CRP, ESR, liver enzyme, bilirubin, glycemia, urea, creatinine, protein, LDH, D-dimer, PT and pH values sit in a sentence with no stated time. Table 1 shows serial values by hospitalization day.

Timing is stated in slightly inconsistent counts: the patient returned "some ten days ago" but was hospitalized on the 8th day after return; doxycycline continued 4 days after return and was stopped on day 5, yet hospitalization is "4 days after he stopped".

Doxycycline adherence rests on the patient report ("according to the patient"); the authors state inadequate dose and poor compliance were excluded after a detailed history, but doxycycline plasma concentration could not be obtained, so prophylaxis failure is not confirmed by drug level.

Table 1 contains N/A (not available) cells for 21 analyte-day values (CRP, AST, ALT on several days and all of RBC, WBC, Hgb, Hct on days 11 and 13 plus AST, ALT, CRP on those days). These are not stated results and are not recorded as observations.
The discussion lists several blood transfusions and fresh frozen plasma transfusions without stating their number, dates or indications.

At discharge the sentence calls the lab results normalized and then lists RBC, Hgb, WBC, CRP, AST, ALT, bilirubin, urea and creatinine values, but only WBC carries its own "within the reference range" phrase. The collective statement is recorded once as normal; individual listed analytes are not flagged normal.

Table 1 hospitalization day 14 values equal several discharge values in the text, but the source does not state that the day 14 row is the discharge sample; text discharge values and Table 1 day 14 cells are kept separate.

Pneumonia was diagnosed by the family physician on day 5 after return and "considered to be atypical"; the hospital chest X-ray showed right lung opacities, but the source does not state whether the pneumonia diagnosis was kept or revised after malaria was confirmed.
